**6h**

# October 9: First Steplings
so... I found out about this club today and I gotta put 13 hours in 2 days, so this might be a tiny bit rushed. This session will be used to document the formation of the project and the goals set.

## Project Description:
This project is for a rc plane where the "cockpit" has a camera allowing me to look through it as if it was irl. The camera angle is controlled by an app, and will hopefully be able to connect to vr later. The body will be custom made and the source of thrust will be from a 100 newton model jet engine.
Example 100 N turbine:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8WQmkKLbXNN01APgAdyJ0e2s2cFNJRsT/40dadcb149608ba52505b2fbbdbea12026115025fc449f4d48d1e826546f18db.png)
very cool very cool

>**Wait, what about safety? and legality?**
If you chose to copy this project, please do it with proper caution and experience. I have made amateur rockets before, and I have always wanted to make a turbine. Additionally, if I had created an electric jet of this caliber, it would last only 3 minutes, but a conventional model jet can last 7 minutes. In the US, making this is no issue, but I would have to be registered in the FAA Dronezone with a TRUST certificate, complete line of sight with a spotter at all times, and an Academy of Model Aeronautics (AMA) turbine waiver. For safety, I will consult with my good friend equipped with knowledge regarding subjects like these and flyers in the AMA.

Anyways, an example plane in this range looks like this:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8WQmkKLbXNN01APgAdyJ0e2s2cFNJRsT/230004625a1f371b108a06f63441b9ff170bfecc5e93d3db3405f493b9a0cd15.png)

Due to this, a conventional wingspan of around 2 meters seems fit (we shall arrange later), guessing the total length to be 80 inches, and by using a 1:1.2 thrust to weight ratio, the plane shall weigh 18 lbs, aiming for a 10 minute flight time. For this weeks goal, I want to create the pcb to be able to control 2 cameras, 12 servos, LEDs, a receiver, a gyro module, a Kerosene glow plug, a solenoid, and a pump like the KP300 BL.

Here's an example of a naked gopro:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8WQmkKLbXNN01APgAdyJ0e2s2cFNJRsT/6758a21428ddf6aea17ee56377c6d089e71348c813b7a0375c2c7ead8b717ef4.png)

## Finally, Research!

after a bit of reading about what's in a flight controller, let's see the constituent pieces:
gah it took me 3.5 hours to find decent information on what is good and what is bad... so little people have a rc plane this fast

Also, I could not journal all the choices I came upon, as it would make this too boring and verbose. Lastly, to elucidate one thing, the goal is to make the pcb, and on week 6, create the turbine.

ECU:
- KP 300 BL, a benchmark pump for now (on a separate 9.9V 3S LiFe battery pack)
- the pcb (of course) with some extra pins for safety
- 6 Feetech DS3115MG, since I cannot use cheap ones due to engine vibration (6.6V, 7.5A)
- Jet-Tronics Single Valve solenoid (6.6V, 130mA) *with a fail close, a hardware kill, bulk capacitance, a TVS diode,  fuses, and it is proven for flight
-TBS Unify Pro32 HV 5.8GHz Video Transmitter (6.6V, 1A)
- 2 naked gopro hero cameras (5V, 4A total)
- 20 lm Red and green wing tip LEDs, 100 lm White LED (7V, guessing 0.5A)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8WQmkKLbXNN01APgAdyJ0e2s2cFNJRsT/2dbc1234c83f6a61cbebbbbadd3933bbb6970acac34f6e193f869bbcb267f688.png)
- Kerosene glow plug a mosfet (1.5-2.5V pwm, ~5, 4A)
- RPM sensor (HAL3021DJ)
- Thermocouple amps (AD8495)

Servo board:
-  4 Spektrum A5070 for rudders, elevators, and taxiing; 4 Spektrum A6320 for flaps and ailerons
- Spektrum AR10410T to power the Spektrum servos and acts as a receiver (3.5-12.6V, 35A continuous)
- Spektrum Synapse AS3X+ (connected to AR10410T)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8WQmkKLbXNN01APgAdyJ0e2s2cFNJRsT/ff0419c4bf50c54364f68505c7ab95f913fb7cdcf956aa68a1923b7f0f18700a.png)

# Making a microcontroller!

So, what made me do this? The rc plen might spark safety concerns even though of my experience, causing me to turn to my other projects, like the PCB creator. Additionally, I wanted a microcontroller for robotics, and buying one with decent performance by myself is quite expensive.

### This session is for finding the pieces for the pcb.
Next will be for routing it

So, let's begin with what we need... To find this, I needed to learn a bunch about college chemistry and Pcb manufacturing, taking around 9 hours itself due to the sheer amount of changing tech. For example, there are at least a thousand **types** of prepregs, which are the "glue" between layers of a pcb.
